# Rhythms and the ECG

[All modules](README.md) · [Known misses](../validation/known-misses.md#rhythms-ecg) · 38 source files, 3482 lines · 45 test files

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
The rhythm engine and ECG generator decide when the atria and ventricles depolarise and draw the resulting ECG: separate
atrial and ventricular clocks with an AV-node state machine, ectopy, pacemaker modes and arrest rhythms, and a
three-axis vectorcardiogram sampled at 500 Hz and projected onto the twelve leads. Each beat also carries the
mechanical output the circulation ejects from. A clinician-educator reads it to see how a rhythm, an electrolyte or an
ischaemic territory shapes the trace; an embedding developer reads it for the beat records and the morphology
modifiers it accepts.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
- The rhythm engine is a discrete-event planner with separate atrial and ventricular clocks joined by an AV-node
  state machine; a ventricle is refractory until QRS + 0.8·QT after it fires (brief §4.1, research 03 §1.5;
  `l2/ecg/rhythm-engine.ts`).
- QT follows Fridericia, QT = QTc·RR^(1/3), and PR shortens by 0.4 ms per bpm above 60 down to 110 ms (research 03
  §1.1; `l2/ecg/intervals.ts`); in Wenckebach the PR lengthens beat by beat as a geometric series (brief §4.1;
  `l2/ecg/atria.ts`).
- Beat-to-beat RR varies as the mean RR plus respiratory sinus arrhythmia, a 0.1 Hz low-frequency term and noise, with
  amplitudes scaled by the mean RR (research 03 §1.4; `l2/ecg/hrv.ts`).
- The ECG on each vectorcardiogram axis is a sum of Gaussian wave kernels per beat, the T wave being two
  half-Gaussians (research 03 §1.3; `l2/ecg/kernels.ts`); the generator adds atrial fibrillation or flutter waves,
  respiratory baseline wander and white noise (brief §3.2, §5; `l2/ecg/generator.ts`).
- Leads I, II and V1–V6 are Dower-matrix projections of the vectorcardiogram, and III, aVR, aVL and aVF follow from the
  Einthoven and Goldberger identities (Dower 1980; research 03 §1.2; `l2/ecg/vcg.ts`).
- ST elevation by territory is an injury vector solved on the Dower rows, so reciprocal change emerges from the
  projection (research 03 §1.6; `l2/ecg/morphology/st.ts`).
- Potassium and temperature alter the morphology in order: peaked T, then P flattening and PR prolongation, then QRS
  widening and a sine wave as potassium rises; U waves and T flattening in hypokalaemia; Osborn J waves in
  hypothermia (brief §5, research 03 §1.6; `l2/ecg/morphology/electrolytes.ts`).
- Ventricular fibrillation's dominant frequency falls from 5.5 Hz towards 3.25 Hz with untreated time, raised by CPR
  and epinephrine, and its amplitude decays exponentially, more slowly during CPR (research 03 §1.8;
  `l2/ecg/arrest/vf.ts`).
- Each beat's mechanical output scales with diastolic filling time, f_fill(RR) = 1 − exp(−(RR − t_sys)/τ_fill),
  normalised to 1 at an RR of 1 s; a non-perfused beat ejects nothing (brief §4.8, research 03 §8.2;
  `l2/ecg/mech.ts`).
- Pacemaker pulses (AAI, VVI, DDD with demand sensing) are marker events rather than sampled spikes (research 03 §1.7;
  `l2/ecg/pacing.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

| `NON_FINITE_FALLBACK_S` | `1` | s | — | A non-finite scheduled time is a physiology bug upstream (a rate of 0/NaN reaching `60 / rate`), and the guard is deliberately ASYMMETRIC. In tests (Vitest sets `NODE_ENV=test`) it THROWS with the value, the clock it came from and the sim time, so the bug is found; everywhere else (the demo, a relay) it clamps that clock to one second after the last planned instant (the 60/min default interval), keeps running and warns ONCE per rhythm state, so an operator never loses the session. ## Known misses

| Target (band) | Measured | Source | Audit verdict | Audit's proposed band | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| amiodarone 150 mg over 10 min: AF 130 slows by 20–30 % at its peak (10–13 min) | 14.0 | — | MIS-SPECIFIED ([audit row 163](../../docs/validation/target-audit/30-target-audit.md#row-163)) | 150 mg over 10 min: rate fall 5-20 % at 10-15 min; add a 300-450 mg arm asserting 25-40 % at 30 min if a strong rate-control band is wanted | [`af-rate-control.test.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/test/engine/af-rate-control.test.ts) |
| sinus 30 + a 40/min junctional focus → 40 QRS/min (escape rhythm, AV dissociation) | 60 | — | TOO NARROW ([audit row 34](../../docs/validation/target-audit/30-target-audit.md#row-34)) | 40-48 QRS/min, junctional beats >= 50 % of QRS, captures allowed (they must come early, after a P falling outside the refractory period) | [`escape-reset.test.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/test/l2/ecg/rhythms/escape-reset.test.ts) |
| never the sum: sinus 30 + a 40/min focus stays below 30 + 40 × ½ (45) QRS/min | 60 | — | MIS-SPECIFIED ([audit row 35](../../docs/validation/target-audit/30-target-audit.md#row-35)) | < 49 for the default (teaching) conduction setting, i.e. most post-escape sinus P waves blocked; model escape-capture bigeminy as an explicit variant, not as the default | [`escape-reset.test.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/test/l2/ecg/rhythms/escape-reset.test.ts) |
